rules.sentence: Laparoscopic appendectomy is indicated in gangrenous non-perforated appendicitis and perforated appendicitis with local contamination.[26][27]
Laparoscopic appendectomy is indicated in gangrenous non-perforated appendicitis and perforated appendicitis with local contamination.[26][27]
When feasible, laparoscopic appendectomy is indicated in patients with perforated appendicitis with generalized peritonitis.
Initial or definitive nonoperative treatment is indicated in patients with a perforated appendix with periappendiceal phlegmon or abscess.[28]
Therefore, in patients with an established diagnosis of Crohn disease without cecal involvement and evidence of acute appendicitis, appendectomy is indicated.[29][30][31][32][33][34]
